subject: Request: graded traffic fallback + version anchor for Atlas Payments SLA
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@atlas-payments.com>, procurement@atlas-payments.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: graded traffic fallback + version anchor for Atlas Payments SLA

Team — quick background: Atlas is finalizing a high-value production contract (see attached SLA draft / MAP). They require a 99.95% uptime SLA for our inference endpoint with strict latency targets for EU checkout traffic. Their legal has asked for our standard rollback/auto-revert guarantees to be documented in the contract, and procurement pushed for a technical mitigation plan.

Given the traffic profile (short, high-request bursts during settlement windows) and the fact they'll be using a 3rd-party CDN in front of our endpoints, we need a short-term operational exception to allow: 1) a graded (2% -> 25%) canary -> ramp A-B for initial rollout with explicit automatic fallback triggers; and 2) the ability to temporarily 'pin' traffic to the prior stable model/version for up to 48 hours while we investigate (i.e., sticky version pin beyond the default auto-unpin window).

Ask: can we get approval for this carveout and the guardrails below so I can (a) confirm to Atlas today and (b) incorporate the language into the SLA/MAP? I attached the SLA draft and a proposed MAP.

High-level proposed guardrails (initial):
- Canary cohort: start at 2% of EU traffic, step to 8% at 15m, 25% at 45m if health checks OK
- Health triggers: p95 latency > 300ms for >5m OR error rate spike >1% => immediate rollback to stable; sustained p95 degradation (over 30m) => auto-pin the prior version for up to 48h
- Auto-pin TTL: 48h max (manual extension requires ops lead + account exec sign-off)
- Telemetry: require request-level traces + per-route token cost + p50/p95/p99 reporting to Atlas for the first 7 days

Attaching: Atlas_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf, MAP_Atlas_2026.xlsx

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0142
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: graded traffic fallback + version anchor for Atlas Payments SLA

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and proposed guardrails. Quick comments before I greenlight the exception: 

1) Thresholds: the p95 300ms trigger seems reasonable for EU checkout but I want the concrete baseline numbers from perf tests (please attach recent perf runs).
2) Visibility: we need a dedicated dashboard for Atlas (token-level cost + latency + errors) and a shared PagerDuty escalation list for the first 72h.
3) Duration and approvals: auto-pin TTL of 48h OK as a default, but we should add an automatic review at 24h and require an SRE + Account Exec sign-off for extension.
4) Legal: ask Atlas to confirm the rollback/pin language is acceptable — Laura_legal prefers the phrase "automatic fallback with temporary version anchoring" and calls out maximum 48h.

Can we map the telemetry thresholds to the MAP milestones (I can sign off once perf baselines are attached and the Atlas PO has confirmed legal language)? Also propose a 30-minute make/break hold window at each ramp step (so we don't escalate on transient blips).

If you want, we can do a 20-minute sync with Karthik and Evelyn today at 16:00 PT to lock down numbers.

-Laura
VP, Product Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: graded traffic fallback + version anchor for Atlas Payments SLA

Laura / Jordan — technical notes and minimal-risk implementation we recommend: 

Implementation summary:
- Canary strategy: progressive ramp (2% -> 8% after 15m -> 25% after 45m) with a 30-minute hold window at each step; step abort on failing health checks.
- Health checks (observable-driven):
  * p95 latency (route-specific) > 320ms for any 5-minute window => abort and immediate rollback
  * 5xx error rate rise > 0.8% absolute (from baseline) over a 5-minute window => abort
  * Token-level error patterns (model errors vs infra errors) must be categorized; infra errors trigger immediate failover
- Auto-pin mechanics:
  * On sustained degradation (p95 > 300ms for 30 minutes OR error rate > 1% for 15 minutes) trigger auto-pin to last stable version
  * Auto-pin TTL: 48 hours; within first 24 hours, system will run a reduced-cadence automated binary search for root-cause (no automatic unpin)
- Safety nets:
  * Immediate circuit-breaker to cut new canary cohort ingress if host-level CPU/GPU throttling observed
  * Cache warm-up recommendation: pre-seed KV cache on canary nodes using synthetic warmup traffic 10m before ramp

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: cascading latency due to cold KV cache during sudden ramp — mitigated by warmup above
- Risk: false-positive p95 spikes from CDN misrouting — mitigated by correlating CDN logs and requiring infra-level errors to escalate

Attachments: I pushed a short rollback_playbook.md to internal docs; attaching a lightweight copy here for the MAP.

If this looks good, I'll prepare an SRE-runbook snippet and the telemetry dashboard template and link them into the MAP/DocuSign packet.

- Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Runtime Reliability
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Rao <anita@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, procurement@atlas-payments.com
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: graded traffic fallback + version anchor for Atlas Payments SLA

Anita — thanks for the patience. Per the internal review above (copied), we can support the graded canary + temporary version anchoring with the guardrails Karthik outlines. Next steps on our side:

- I will update the MAP and SLA language to include the precise rollback triggers and the 48h anchor TTL, with a 24h review clause.
- We will provision a shared Atlas dashboard (token-level cost, p50/p95/p99, errors) and a PagerDuty escalation list for the first 72h.
- Karthik will hand off the runbook and warmup plan; we recommend Atlas schedule the initial cutover for a low-traffic window and allow pre-seeding KV cache 10m prior.

Please confirm the legal wording below is acceptable and we will push the DocuSign packet: 
"Redwood will implement a graded canary rollout for production traffic to Atlas endpoints with an automatic fallback to the last stable model on detection of significant performance regression. In cases of sustained degradation, Redwood reserves the right to temporarily anchor traffic to the previously stable model for up to forty-eight (48) hours while investigation proceeds. Extensions require mutual written agreement."

If that looks good, I will send the DocuSign link this afternoon and lock the tentative cutover for next Tuesday (EU low-traffic window).

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
